title: Gaussian best-arm identification: fixed budget and static-allocation exponent comparison
summary: The algorithm samples Gaussian arms under a fixed budget and recommends the best arm without knowing the instance's optimal static allocation. The comparison is between the asymptotic error exponent and the instance-informed static-allocation benchmark, with one algorithm sequence required to work on every instance.

description_paragraphs: The algorithm samples Gaussian arms under a fixed budget and recommends the best arm without knowing the instance's optimal static allocation. The comparison is between the asymptotic error exponent and the instance-informed static-allocation benchmark, with one algorithm sequence required to work on every instance.

model.instance: Arm $i$ has distribution $\nu_i=N(\mu_i,1)$, with $\mu\in\mathbb R^K$ and a unique best arm. For each fixed budget $T$, recommend after exactly $T$ fresh samples. Consider algorithm families $(A_T)$ whose error tends to zero on every admissible $\mu$, and compare asymptotic difficulty relative to the static allocation oracle that knows the instance.

model.parameter_domain_description: K: $K\in\mathbb N,\ K\ge2$ (public); T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public)
interaction_timing: Fix mu; A_T receives public K, T, and variance one.
Choose arms from the history and receive Gaussian samples sequentially until exactly $T$ samples have been taken.
Return a recommendation and define its error probability p_{μ,T}.
First take the limsup as T tends to infinity for fixed mu, then the supremum over mu, and finally the infimum over uniform algorithm families.
model.adversary_information: The unknown distribution or parameter is fixed before interaction. Learner randomness and sample randomness are independent. No adversary changes the distribution round by round from the learner's history.
unresolved_applicability: The verified result is a lower bound on uniform relative asymptotic difficulty, not a uniformly optimal formula for every finite-budget error probability on one instance.
description_paragraphs: The Gaussian means $\mu$ are unknown. Variance is known and equals one; no common bounded interval is imposed on the means.
The algorithm family is $\mathcal{A}=(\mathcal{A}_T)_{T\ge1}$, with each $\mathcal{A}_T$ given the budget $T$. Consistency requires $p_{\mu,T}\to0$ for every admissible mean vector $\mu$.

The asymptotic static-oracle benchmark is $H_{\mathrm{so}}(\mu)$. Its optimal allocation may depend on the true means, which remain hidden from the learner. The natural exponential-family definition uses reverse divergence $\operatorname{KL}(\nu_{\lambda_i}\|\nu_{\mu_i})$; for unit-variance Gaussians it equals half the squared mean difference.
The model requires $K\ge2$, with algorithm budgets $T\ge1$. The registered nontrivial impossibility bound additionally requires $K\ge3$, which remains explicit in its region.

The set $\Delta_K^\circ$ is the probability simplex with strictly positive coordinates. In the alternative set $\operatorname{Alt}(\mu)$, the original best arm may tie with another arm or cease to be optimal.

public_inputs: Budget T for each algorithm A_T
auxiliary_interfaces: No additional oracle reveals means, gaps, optimal sampling proportions, or posteriors. Statistics, likelihood ratios, and allocation optimizations are computed internally from observed samples and the public model.
description_paragraphs: Sampling Gaussian arms with known variance:

$$
t\in[T],\quad a_t\in[K]\ \longmapsto\ Y_t=\mu_{a_t}+Z_t,\qquad Z_t\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)
$$
Each call draws an independent fresh sample. The noise $Z_t$ is independent of the pre-selection history and private algorithmic randomness.
Optimal static sampling proportions, μ, and gaps are not supplied.
Recommend after using the budget. There is no stopping-time optimization or cumulative-regret objective.
Public inputs are arm count $K$, the current algorithm $\mathcal A_T$'s budget $T$, and the promise of unit Gaussian variance.

output.feasibility: Recommend one arm in $[K]$. Stopping and fixed-budget rules follow the declared protocol.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
description_paragraphs: After at most $T$ samples, return a recommended arm $\widehat{b}_T\in[K]$. Any postprocessing of the observed history is allowed. The arm need not have been sampled, and no additional certificate is required.

metric.normalization: The benchmark is the static-oracle difficulty H_so(μ) when μ is known. The objective is a dimensionless asymptotic ratio based on log(1/p_error), not the raw finite-horizon error probability.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The mean vector mu has a unique best arm and H_so(mu) lies in (0,infinity). Define T/log(1/p) as zero at p=0 and positive infinity at p=1, allowing extended-real values.
description_paragraphs:
$$
p_{\mu,T}(\mathcal{A}_T)=\mathbb{P}_\mu(\widehat{b}_T\ne b(\mu)),\quad H_{\mathrm{so}}(\mu)^{-1}=\sup_{w\in\Delta_K^\circ}\inf_{\lambda\in\mathrm{Alt}(\mu)}\frac12\sum_i w_i(\lambda_i-\mu_i)^2
$$

description_paragraphs: An algorithm with budget $T$ takes exactly $T$ samples. This comparison studies its error exponent relative to instance difficulty as $T\to\infty$.
The algorithm family must satisfy the guarantee uniformly instancewise. Polynomial time and knowledge of a gap are not assumed.
For error probability $p=0$, define $T/\log(1/p)=0$; for $p=1$, define it as $+\infty$.
Error probability already includes algorithm randomness and sample noise. No additional unspecified expectation is applied outside the criterion.

Information calls, arithmetic, communication rounds, and memory are measured separately. Exact real internal computation is excluded from information complexity unless explicitly charged. This does not imply a bit-complexity bound.

algorithms.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
algorithms.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: The family $A=(A_T)_{T\ge1}$ is instancewise consistent: $p_{\mu,T}(A_T)\to0$ for every admissible $\mu$. Each $A_T$ may know $T$, but not $\mu$ or the static oracle allocation.
algorithms.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable exact-real internal computation is allowed; feedback complexity implies no arithmetic or bit bound. The algorithm family must be instancewise consistent; polynomial time and known gaps are not assumed. Interpret T/log(1/p) as zero at p=0 and as positive infinity at p=1. Probabilities already integrate algorithmic and sample randomness, so no unspecified outer expectation is added.
algorithms.parallelism: Interaction proceeds in sequential time rounds. A two-point evaluation is one pair of same-round responses only where explicitly permitted; it is not equivalent to two independent rounds.
description_paragraphs: All measurable causal randomized policies respecting the stated timing are allowed. The private seed is independent of the fixed instance and future samples. Apart from explicit feedback, output, and budget requirements, there are no restrictions on linear spans, iteration form, internal arithmetic, memory, or communication.

guarantees.complete_expression: The native target is $\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{cons}}}\sup_{\mu:\ b(\mu)\ \mathrm{unique}}\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{T}{H_{\mathrm{so}}(\mu)\log(1/p_{\mu,T}(\mathcal A_T))}$.
aggregation_order: For each fixed μ, first integrate algorithmic and sampling randomness into the error probability p_{μ,T}.
Fix $\mu$ and take the asymptotic limsup of the relative difficulty as $T\to\infty$.
Then take the supremum over μ. The outermost infimum ranges over entire algorithm families that are consistent instance by instance.
Do not interchange $\sup_\mu$ and $\limsup_T$, or replace the asymptotic statement by a uniform finite-$T$ error-probability bound.
guarantees.quantifier_order: One algorithm must work for every μ. Static oracle may know μ only as a benchmark, not as learner input.
guarantees.time_uniformity: Each T specifies a separate fixed-budget algorithm A_T; the asymptotic comparison uses the complete uniform algorithm family.
description_paragraphs: Choose one fixed-budget algorithm family $\{\mathcal{A}_T\}_{T\ge1}$, then take the worst case over fixed unknown Gaussian means with a unique best arm. For each instance first let $T\to\infty$, and compare its error exponent with the static-allocation benchmark. This is neither finite-$T$ error probability nor a fixed-confidence sample count.

quantities.expression_latex: \begin{aligned} \rho_K^*&=\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathcal C_{\rm cons}}\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal M_K}\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{T}{H_{\rm so}(\mu)\log(1/p_{\mu,T}(\mathcal A_T))},\\ p_{\mu,T}(\mathcal A_T)&=\mathbb P_{\mu,\mathcal A_T}(\widehat b_T\ne b(\mu)),\\ \mathcal C_{\rm cons}&=\{(\mathcal A_T)_{T\ge1}:\ \forall\mu\in\mathcal M_K,\ p_{\mu,T}(\mathcal A_T)\to0\},\\ \mathcal M_K&=\{\mu\in\mathbb R^K:\ b(\mu)\text{ is unique}\}.\end{aligned}

conditions: Fix $K\ge3$, assume a unique best arm, unknown means, and known unit Gaussian variance, and consider $T\to\infty$.

The lower bound covers consistent policies. Preserve the order of quantifiers and limits in $\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_\mu\limsup_{T\to\infty}$. Do not interchange the worst-instance operation and asymptotic limit or extend the claim to arbitrary inconsistent fixed-budget policies.

evidence.supports: Supports the stated results and explicit reductions: $\begin{aligned}[c]\rho_K^*&\ge1+\sum_{j=3}^K(1+\sqrt{j-1})^{-2}>1+\frac{\log K}{8},\\ H_{\rm so}(\mu)^{-1}&=\sup_{w\in\Delta_K^\circ}\inf_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}(\mu)}\sum_{i=1}^K w_i\operatorname{KL}\bigl(N(\lambda_i,1)\,\|\,N(\mu_i,1)\bigr).\end{aligned}$. Each bound retains its own model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: Gaussian variance is one, and algorithms are restricted to consistent fixed-budget policies. The source orders the limit and worst-instance operations as $$\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_\mu\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{T}{H_{\mathrm{so}}(\mu)\log(1/p_{\mu,T})}\ge1+\sum_{j=3}^K(1+\sqrt{j-1})^{-2}.$$. Static-oracle complexity uses reverse KL and is distinct from the fixed-confidence characteristic time.
